title: What this means for energy traders — Thursday, November 5, 2026

sections.overall: Politics and the Iran war dominate the headlines. Oil sold off after the US midterms and on talk of diplomacy with Iran, while the corporate trend ledger is quiet: all three confirmed trends are STEADY, with no company activity counted this week against last. The news flow is event-driven, not driven by a rally behind any one corporate idea.
sections.CRUDE_OIL: CNBC reported crude falling below $90 a barrel on Wednesday after the midterm losses, following a Nov. 2 drop in Brent to $105.55 on hopes of an end to the Iran war (CNBC, The Guardian). Markets typically treat diplomatic headlines as a reduction in supply-risk premium, though the stories don't show whether the talks have produced anything concrete. Producers keep posting strong volumes, as in CNOOC's reported record January–September output, which is a reminder that supply-side news continues alongside the geopolitics.
sections.NATURAL_GAS: LNG deal flow continues across regions. TotalEnergies signed a heads of agreement with Jiangsu Guoxin, and XRG moved into Australian LNG, both fitting the confirmed Asia-offtake trend (LNG Prime). The FT headlines on Qatar as a large buyer of US LNG and on Germany missing its storage target point to both long-term contracting and near-term European balancing. A preliminary heads of agreement is generally treated as a weaker signal than a binding contract.
sections.REFINED_PRODUCTS: The EIA says refiners shifted yields from gasoline toward distillates, consistent with strong distillate and jet margins (EIA). The FT headline says US fuel supplies hit a 20-year low and that the Russian diesel arrangement is faltering. Tight distillate availability is commonly read as supportive of cracks, while any diplomatic progress is read in the opposite direction. How the two balance out is unclear.
sections.CARBON_CREDITS: Demand for removals remains a theme: a Carbon Pulse report headline says demand far outstrips supply, and Robinson Carbon is adding biochar capacity. Policy headlines include EU ETS and ETS2 reform pressure from Poland and Czechia, and Verra's first ICVCM approval for coal-retirement transition credits. EUAs fell in thin trading after a US equity sell-off, per Carbon Pulse's headline.
